responses.prompt:
Task: Pick one query template that would confirm this risk, and give the values of its parameters. The templates are: osv-by-package (ecosystem: one of Go, npm, PyPI, package: a package name in the ecosystem's own spelling) gives the OSV advisory rows of one package. osv-by-advisory (advisory_id: an advisory id such as GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx or GO-2021-0113) gives the OSV advisory with one advisory id. kev-by-cve (cve_id: a CVE id such as CVE-2021-44228) gives the CISA known-exploited entry of one CVE. epss-by-cve (cve_id: a CVE id such as CVE-2021-44228) gives the EPSS score of one CVE. Do not write SQL: Proven builds the query from the template. Leave template empty when none fits. Do not treat a missing row as not exploited.

Reply with JSON only.

The JSON is one JSON object. It has template (string) and params (an object of strings).

Example:
{"template":"kev-by-cve","params":{"cve_id":"CVE-2021-44228"}}

Task: Make one attempt to refute this finding. A refuting query is one of these templates with the values of its parameters: osv-by-package (ecosystem: one of Go, npm, PyPI, package: a package name in the ecosystem's own spelling) gives the OSV advisory rows of one package. osv-by-advisory (advisory_id: an advisory id such as GHSA-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx or GO-2021-0113) gives the OSV advisory with one advisory id. kev-by-cve (cve_id: a CVE id such as CVE-2021-44228) gives the CISA known-exploited entry of one CVE. epss-by-cve (cve_id: a CVE id such as CVE-2021-44228) gives the EPSS score of one CVE.

Do not add a command or SQL: Proven builds the command that runs the test and the SQL of the query.

Example:
